reading: Every solid square of side n is replaced by a concentric square of side n-2 in the same colour (a 3x3 becomes its centre cell); a single cell instead grows into a 9x9 square centred on it.

slots.subject: each solid single-colour square object
slots.change: side n -> n-2 concentric (same centre); side 1 -> side 9

why: every output object is a concentric square of the input square's colour with side n-2 (or 9 when n=1)

reading: Each object loses its two leftmost columns (those cells become background).

new_rows.name: trim
new_rows.datalog:
minx(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
trim(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), minx(O, M), D = X - M, D < 2.

why: every cell of an object within two columns of its leftmost column becomes background 8; nothing else changes

reading: Two single-colour shapes (rectangles or lines) overlap; the shape that was partly hidden is brought to the front, so the overlap cells take the hidden shape's colour.

slots.back: the shape whose outline is interrupted by the other
slots.overlap: cells of the front shape lying on the back shape's completed outline

why: only overlap cells change, and each takes the colour of the shape that was occluded

reading: Each colour-4 rectangle holds k single marks of one colour c; a solid ring of colour c and thickness k is drawn around the rectangle.

slots.subject: each 4-rectangle with marks inside
slots.colour: the colour of its inner marks
slots.region: background cells within Chebyshev distance thickness of the rectangle's box

why: around every rectangle the band of width k (k = mark count) is filled with the mark colour; the rectangle itself is unchanged

reading: Plus-shaped objects whose centres lie on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal line of colour 2 through the background cells between them.

new_rows.name: diag
new_rows.datalog:
ctr(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Ya = Y - 1, cell(Ya, X, C), Yb = Y + 1, cell(Yb, X, C), Xa = X - 1, cell(Y, Xa, C), Xb = X + 1, cell(Y, Xb, C).
diag(Y, X) :- ctr(Y1, X1), ctr(Y2, X2), px(Y, X, 0), D = Y2 - Y1, E = X2 - X1, D = E, D > 1, Y > Y1, Y < Y2, F = Y - Y1, G = X - X1, F = G.
diag(Y, X) :- ctr(Y1, X1), ctr(Y2, X2), px(Y, X, 0), D = Y2 - Y1, E = X1 - X2, D = E, D > 1, Y > Y1, Y < Y2, F = Y - Y1, G = X1 - X, F = G.

why: every background cell on the diagonal segment between two plus centres becomes 2; nothing else changes

reading: Each solid object moves straight up by a distance equal to its own height.

slots.subject: each object
slots.distance: the object's own height (rows of its box)

why: every object keeps shape and colour and its box shifts up by exactly its height

reading: The whole grid is painted with its most common colour.
why: every non-majority cell takes the majority (background) colour

reading: A hub of colour 9 stays fixed; each other-coloured piece attached to it slides straight away from the 9 cell it touches until it reaches the grid border, keeping its shape.
verb: push pieces away from hub to border

new_rows.name: piece
new_rows.datalog: piece(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C < 9.

why: every non-9 piece keeps its shape and ends touching the border on the side facing away from the adjacent 9 cell

reading: The colour-3 shape moves straight toward the full colour-2 line until it touches it, then a full line of colour 8 is drawn on the shape's far side, parallel to the 2 line.

new_rows.name: far
new_rows.datalog:
top3(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, 3).
bot3(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, 3).
lft3(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, 3).
rgt3(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, 3).
hsep(Y) :- cell(Y, X, 2), X2 = X + 1, cell(Y, X2, 2).
vsep(X) :- cell(Y, X, 2), Y2 = Y + 1, cell(Y2, X, 2).
far(Y, X) :- hsep(S), top3(T), S > T, Y = T - 1, px(Y, X, C).
far(Y, X) :- hsep(S), bot3(B), S < B, Y = B + 1, px(Y, X, C).
far(Y, X) :- vsep(S), lft3(L), S > L, X = L - 1, px(Y, X, C).
far(Y, X) :- vsep(S), rgt3(R), S < R, X = R + 1, px(Y, X, C).

why: the 3 shape keeps its shape and ends in contact with the 2 line; the full line adjacent to its opposite side is 8

reading: A 2x2 colour key sits in a corner beside a square field of one-colour cells; the field is split into four quadrants and every coloured cell takes the key colour of its quadrant.

slots.key: the 2x2 multi-coloured block in the corner
slots.field: the square background area bounded by the 8 strips
slots.subject: the field's coloured cells
slots.map: cell in quadrant (i,j) of the field -> key[i][j]

why: every field cell of the mark colour becomes the key colour at the same relative quadrant; nothing else changes
